from.place: proof, diagonal step: the diagonal of a smooth morphism is a regular immersion of codimension d

title: The diagonal of a smooth separated morphism is a regular immersion
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let f:X\to S be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] morphism of pure relative dimension d whose diagonal \Delta:X\to X\times_S X [def-pc-base-change] is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then every point of X\times_S X has an affine open neighbourhood U=\operatorname{Spec}A such that the ideal I\subset A of \Delta^{-1}(U) is either A or is generated by an A-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] f_1,\dots,f_d of length d.

source.place: Tag 067U, Lemma 31.22.11 (an immersion between schemes smooth over S is a regular immersion), applied to \Delta, a section of the smooth projection p_1 of relative dimension d

proof.text: Let $w\in X\times_S X$ lie outside the closed image of $\Delta$. Its open complement contains an affine open neighbourhood $U$ of $w$. Then $\Delta^{-1}(U)$ is empty, so its ideal in $\mathcal O(U)$ is the unit ideal. This is the first alternative in the statement.

source.place: Tag 067R, proof: restrict to the image and its open complement

proof.text: Now let $w=\Delta(x)$ and suppose $d=0$. By the last sentence of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $f$ is etale; by [def-weil-etale-morphism] it is unramified. The definition [def-weil-unramified-morphism] says directly that its diagonal $\Delta$ is an open immersion. It is also a closed immersion by hypothesis. Hence its image is open and closed, and an affine open $U$ containing $w$ can be chosen inside that image. On $U$ the diagonal is an isomorphism, so its ideal is zero, generated by the empty regular sequence of length $0$.

source.place: Tag 067R, section case; dimension-zero etale case

proof.text: Suppose $d>0$. Apply [lem-sc-standard-smooth-local-relative-dimension] at $x$ to choose affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $X$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $S$, with $x\in V$, $f(V)\subseteq T$, and $R\to A$ standard smooth of relative dimension $d$. The open subscheme $V\times_T V$ of $X\times_S X$ contains $w$, and the restriction of $\Delta$ to it is the affine diagonal of $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ (by the fibre-product universal property).

source.place: Tags 02G2 and 054L; restriction of the diagonal to affine charts

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-standard-smooth-affine-diagonal-generators] to the standard-smooth map $R\to A$ and the diagonal point $w$. It supplies an affine neighbourhood $U$ within $V\times_T V$ on which the ideal of the restricted diagonal is generated by a regular sequence of length $d$. Since $V\times_T V$ is open in $X\times_S X$ and the restricted diagonal is its pullback, the same $U$ and ideal give the required neighbourhood for the original diagonal.

source.place: Tag 067R; standard-smooth affine diagonal calculation in WeilConjectures/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/RegularImmersion.lean:336-375
